# TW1 Data Health Checkup - Audit Summary (auto-generated)

Source file: B2B SaaS Churn Data.xlsx | Generated by tw1_data_health_audit.py
All figures below are computed from the raw extract; nothing has been cleaned or removed.

## Part 1 - High-Level Data Health Audit

### 1. Volume & Redundancy
- IT claimed **2,500** records; the file contains **2,510** rows (+10).
- **9** rows are exact duplicates of another row.
- **10** rows repeat an existing Customer_ID; 1 Customer_ID(s) appear with conflicting field values (same ID, different data).
- Unique customers: **2,500**. After de-duplicating on Customer_ID the table holds 2,500 rows.

### 2. Schema & Format Inconsistencies
- Numeric columns stored as text in Excel: **0** cells. Monthly_Revenue is numeric, but only **378** cells carry a `$` currency display format while the rest are plain numbers, so the column looks mixed in Excel and would break if anyone re-typed it as text.
- Industry: **12** raw spellings collapse to **6** real industries; **251** rows use lower-case variants (e.g. `retail` vs `Retail`). Any pivot or model treats these as separate segments.
- Churn_Label mixes text and numbers: {'No': 1974, 'Yes': 486, '1': 50} - **50** rows are encoded as a number instead of Yes/No. The numeric code is NOT a safe synonym for "Yes": every `Yes` row has a Date_Cancelled (486 of 486), but only **7** of the 50 numeric rows do. These rows need to be resolved against Date_Cancelled (or confirmed with IT), not blindly recoded.
- Contract_Type contains **50** rows labelled `Unknown`.
- Missing values: Support_Tickets is blank in **125** rows; Date_Cancelled is blank in 2,017 rows (expected - blank means the customer has not cancelled).

### 3. Logical Errors & Impossible Values
- Negative Total_Users: **1** row(s); negative Monthly_Revenue: **1** row(s); negative Last_Login_Days_Ago: **50** rows; negative Support_Tickets: 0.
- Churn label vs. cancel date: 43 churned rows without a Date_Cancelled; 0 non-churned rows with a Date_Cancelled; 0 rows cancelled before they joined.
- Join_Date spans 2020-01-01 to 2022-12-31; Date_Cancelled spans 2022-01-07 to 2023-12-28.

### 4. Extreme Outliers
- Monthly_Revenue whale(s) at or above $100,000: **1** row(s) (Customer_ID [1051]). Raw mean = **$1,381.36** vs. **$983.35** without the whale (median $803.50). The single record inflates the average by about $398.01.
- Total_Users at or above 10,000: **1** row(s) (Customer_ID [1061]). Raw mean = 39.28 users vs. 19.37 without it (median 16.0).
- See sheet `Outlier_IQR_Screen` for a 3x IQR fence on every numeric column.

### 5. Cross-field consistency (beyond the four required checks)
- Pricing sanity: typical accounts pay about **$50.8 per user per month** (range 36.0 to 99.0). The whale row implies $58,824 per user and the 50,000-user row implies $0.02 per user, i.e. both are roughly 1,000x off the pricing pattern. This confirms they are data-entry errors (an extra "000"), not real strategic accounts, and identifies which field is wrong in each row. 2 rows fall outside the $20-$150 per-user band (sheet `Consist_RevPerUser`).
- Engagement field is not time-anchored: the extract runs to 2023-12-28, yet **470 of 493** cancelled customers show a Last_Login_Days_Ago that would place their last login AFTER they cancelled (every value is 0-30 days regardless of when the account left). Last_Login_Days_Ago was evidently measured at a different point in time per customer, or generated without reference to cancellation, so it cannot be used as-is as an early-warning signal.
- Support_Tickets blanks look random rather than systematic: missing share is 5.4% vs 4.9% for churned vs. retained customers and 3.6% to 6.9% across industries. This supports simple imputation plus a missing flag instead of dropping rows.
- History window: customers joined in {2020: 857, 2021: 806, 2022: 847} but cancellations exist only for {2022: 145, 2023: 348}. Either churn before 2022 was purged from the extract (survivorship bias in the 2022 base) or the file only tracks two years of exits; confirm with IT before quoting a multi-year trend.
- Company_Name is derived from Customer_ID (`Company_<ID-1001>`, derived for all rows = True); it carries no information and should be treated as an identifier, not a feature.

## Part 2 support - Descriptive & Diagnostic numbers (per unique customer)
- Churn events by cancellation year: **2022 = 145** (8.8% of customers active at the start of 2022) vs. **2023 = 346** (14.7% of customers active at the start of 2023). Churn events roughly 2.4x year over year; the data supports the VP's concern. Overall churn = 21.4% of unique customers.
- Simple Excel-style view (share of all 2,500 customers): 2022 = 5.8%, 2023 = 13.8%.
- Largest segment: **Retail** (17.8% of customers). Highest churn industry: Education (24.2%).
- Contract type: **Month-to-Month** churns most (33.7%), **2 Year** least (15.3%). Full tables in sheets `P2_*`.
- Note: churn rates by year use the cleaned Yes/No label and de-duplicated customers; the "rate" denominator is customers who had joined before Jan 1 of that year and had not yet cancelled.

## Part 3 support - Data Leakage evidence
- Date_Cancelled is populated for **491** churned customers and for **0** retained customers: it is a one-to-one proxy for Churn_Label and is only known AFTER the customer has left. It must be dropped (or used only to build the label / churn-year) before modelling. See sheet `P3_LeakageCrosstab`.
- Last_Login_Days_Ago is measured at extract time, not at the decision point, so it is a softer leakage risk and should be time-anchored in a production pipeline.
